title: Is an agent run getting more expensive day by day? Research runs grew about 5% a day in cost and tool calls, other tracks did not
lede: on 1,053 priced run records (16 to 21 October 2026) the median research run grew about 4.9% a day in API-equivalent cost (95% interval +2.8 to +7.0) and 5.7% a day in tool calls, while cost per call stayed flat; ventures runs show no drift (preliminary, observational, six days)
summary: Run cost is what limits the loop's throughput, so a rising cost per run would eat the budget silently. This project fits a Theil-Sen trend (the median of pairwise slopes, robust to the long cost tail) to log cost, log cost per tool call and log tool calls against start date, with a percentile bootstrap over runs, for 1,053 run records that carry cost_usd, tool_calls and a start time. Pooled, cost per run rises 3.4% a day (95% interval +1.2 to +5.1). That is a research effect: research runs (456) rise 4.9% a day in cost (+2.8 to +7.0) and 5.7% a day in tool calls (+3.9 to +7.8) while cost per call is flat (−0.5%, −1.1 to +0.1), so research runs are doing more steps, not paying more per step. Ventures, process, red-team, explore and review runs have intervals that include zero for cost per run. The median research run cost $0.88 on 16 October and $1.05 on 21 October. Limits: six calendar days, of which 21 October is partial; observational, so the data cannot say whether the brief, the portfolio's growth or the task mix caused the rise; cost is API-equivalent from tokens, not a bill; the bootstrap treats runs as independent although concurrent runs share a day.
